# Qualified AdES CLI fixture cases

These complete inputs were freshly generated by running the unchanged eight
pyHanko0.38.1 CLI AdES tests with certvalidator0.33.0; all11 parameter executions
passed. `prepare.py` is the small external pytest plugin that copies each actual
isolated filesystem after original assertions and before teardown. `cases.txt`
records the exact parameter order. Upstream fixtures are MIT-licensed.

Original logical clock is recorded per case in `original-clock.txt` and
`moment.txt`. This fresh run used the real fixture timezone America/Los_Angeles:
2020-08-01T00:00-07:00, equivalent to2020-08-01T07:00Z. The native tests use the
existing explicit `run_with_runtime` test seam at that actual original instant. Their fresh same-input Python peer uses the same original freezegun
clock. No native product NOW/validation clock override is introduced or claimed.
The final original explicitly requests2025-03-01T22:00Z and no revocation check;
that mode remains a real full-LTA call rather than a Basic/status-only fallback.

Each case contains the actual signed LTA PDF, signed TL/LOTL cache, configured
TLSO/root certificates and YAML. Cache `index.json` is an application input,
not a provenance/evidence artifact. Its seeded3650day expiry is the original
fixture behavior; production cache refresh remains15days. No service clocks,
certificate validity or already-signed PDF bytes were retimed to create a result.

The eight Rust functions retain all original assertions, including the four
`overloaded_trust × pades_style` cases. The mandatory nonqualified rejection is
preceded by genuine qualified-required and SAME-input nonqualified-optional
positives, so an always-untrusted/unsupported implementation cannot pass it.
Tests retain the final full-LTA subindication and actual CMS/qualification status;
reference display text does not replace mandatory native trust requirements.

The2025/no-revinfo original is explicitly ignored with its complete assertions
retained. Actual native fullLTA returns NO_POE/INVALID because no historical
control time can be established for the expired leaf; pinned Python CLI accepts
the projected API status. The native full-LTA gate remains intact. The other
seven originals retain genuine fullLTA positive and mandatory-negative checks.

The same-input original CLI peer also enters the upstream `live_pki_services`
context with the genuine qualified test PKI, exactly as the original fixture.
Python needs those live signed revocation responses during its current-time
validation stage. Native LTA uses its authenticated embedded evidence offline.
The comparison therefore retains the same PDF/config/TL inputs and original
clock, with different represented retrieval sources; it does not claim identical
revocation-acquisition traces. No response/status/POE is fabricated.
